_comment: FlowHub configuration, version 2: which event sources exist, what starting work means for each, which agent runtimes are declared, and which local repository each (source, project) pair drives.
_comment_usage: Copy to ~/.config/flowhub/config.json ($XDG_CONFIG_HOME/flowhub/config.json when set) and replace every placeholder below; that is the default path, and FLOWHUB_CONFIG_FILE overrides it (FLOWHUB_PROJECTS_FILE still works). This file in the repository is NOT loaded by default.
_comment_version: Version 1 was the original routing table: `projects[].youtrack_key`, one global key index, every source fact in the environment. A file with no `version` key is still read, translated, and reported as `1 (translated; migrate the file to version 2)`. A version 2 file that uses a version 1 spelling is refused with the replacement named.
_comment_secrets: No secret belongs in this file. Locks and key material stay in the environment — FLOWHUB_YOUTRACK_HOOK_KEY, FLOWHUB_YOUTRACK_TOKEN, FLOWHUB_YOUTRACK_ALLOWED_SOURCES (the unsuffixed names still work for YouTrack) — so this file stays safe to copy, diff, back up and review. A runtime's credentials are named by the variable that holds them (see auth below), never written out.
_comment_startup: Validation runs before any file is created, and a problem stops the process: an unknown version, an unknown field, a source this binary cannot build, a runtime block that cannot be honoured, a duplicate (source, project), a missing or relative repo.path, a malformed agent or model reference. The *filesystem* checks — does the repository exist, is it a git work tree, is its origin the declared one, does the checkout directory sit outside it — belong to the workspace provider and run in the same gate.
_comment_report: `flowhub -print-config` prints each effective value with the level that supplied it (`effective: sources.youtrack trigger=... (level: FLOWHUB_TRIGGER)`), which is how a three-level file stays answerable.

sources._comment: Keyed by the adapter's own name. `enabled` defaults to true, and a source the file never mentions is enabled: the hook key is the lock, and a record-only receiver should not need the file at all. `policy` holds what starting work means for this tracker; every field is optional and the environment is the outermost default. `prompt_file` is parsed but refused as not implemented yet — the adapter's built-in prompt is used, and a declared file that silently did nothing would be worse.

policy._comment: trigger must match the whole first line (it is anchored). start_states are the workflow states that mean the same thing. max_turns is the runaway guard. self_markers identify FlowHub's own replies when the marker inside the text is lost. FLOWHUB_TRIGGER / FLOWHUB_START_STATES / FLOWHUB_SKIP_ANALYZE_ON_CREATE / FLOWHUB_MAX_TURNS are the same values at the outermost level; whatever this block names wins.

youtrack._comment_authors: Optional source-level author allowlist (tracker logins, case-insensitive), inherited by every project of this source. A project may narrow it further; a project without its own list allows everyone this source allows.
youtrack._comment_prompt_file: Optional path to a file of extra instructions for this source's turns, resolved relative to this file. It is *appended* to the adapter's built-in prompt, never a replacement: the untrusted-input warning, the reply tool, the sign-off and the <!-- flowhub-auto --> marker are the adapter's contract and a text file must not be able to delete them. A missing, empty, directory or >32 KiB file refuses the start rather than quietly doing nothing.

runtimes._comment: Keyed by the enrolled runtime's name. This table is policy, not enrolment: the control-plane inventory (ADR 0002, `flowhub runtime invite` / `init`) records which hosts were prepared and verified, their state and the models they reported, while this says what to ask of them. A name that appears only here is a local runtime — usable without enrolment, which is the single-host case FLOWHUB_OPENCODE_URL used to be the only way to express.

local._comment_url: Where the host's agent server listens. Omit it and the runtime is only usable if the inventory enrols it. FLOWHUB_OPENCODE_URL is the outermost default.
local._comment_auth: HTTP Basic Auth, which is what makes a runtime reachable across a network instead of only over loopback. The secret stays in the environment and this block only names the variable; an empty variable, or a user without a password_env (or the reverse), refuses the start. FLOWHUB_OPENCODE_USER/PASSWORD are the outermost default.
local._comment_agent: The agent profile inside that product. Never the product name: asking opencode for an agent called "opencode" makes its server fall back to its own default agent, which is a looser one.
local._comment_model: Optional. Pinning it here wins over the model the host reported at enrolment; leave it empty to use what the host reported, and a project entry can still override both.
local._comment_deadline: One turn's budget on this host. FLOWHUB_TASK_DEADLINE is the outermost default.
local._comment_max_concurrent: Only 1 is accepted. A session belongs to one runtime and a prompt sent to a busy session is silently swallowed, so raising this needs per-task locking that does not exist yet.

projects._comment: One entry per (source, project) pair. The same project key in two sources is two entries; the same key twice in one source is refused. `also` lets several tracker projects share one repository. `runtime`/`runtimes` is an eligibility set, not a preference list; `runtime_policy` decides how a new task picks within it. A task that is already bound to a runtime stays there for life.

repo._comment: path is the local clone the workspace provider prepares tasks from: absolute, canonicalised on load (symlinks resolved), because the runtime treats /tmp and /private/tmp as different projects. remote is compared against .git/config so a typo cannot route work into the wrong clone. default_branch is resolved through the origin to a commit when a task is created, and that commit is pinned for the task's life.

projects._comment_prompt_file: Optional per-project instructions, appended after the source's. This is where a repository says "this repo is Java, run `mvn -q verify`"; it is read at load time like the source's and refused the same way if it is unusable.
projects._comment_worktrees: Base directory for the one-checkout-per-task isolation. Absolute, outside repo.path, created on demand. Required once dispatch is on (FLOWHUB_DISPATCH=1) unless FLOWHUB_WORKTREE_BASE provides the fallback.
projects._comment_overrides: agent and model override the runtime block for this project only; authors is a per-project allowlist; enabled defaults to true, and a disabled entry is never matched and not validated.
